transcript.text: Hello, I'm Peter Hale, sixty-six, from Edinburgh. I retired from the police and opened a small pub in Chengdu. We serve whisky with rabbit heads. That pairing raises a few eyebrows, usually mine first. After a long working life, I rather enjoy a quiet bar and a good conversation.
你好，我叫彼得·黑尔，爱丁堡人，今年六十六岁。我以前在苏格兰当警察，退休以后来成都开了间小酒馆。我们卖威士忌，也卖兔头。第一次听的人都觉得奇怪，吃过以后，有人会再来一份。
Take that chair by the window. It's the quietest spot. There's no rush to order. Tell me what sort of evening you've had, and we'll find you something suitable.
Well, look who's come through the door! I thought you were still in Edinburgh. Give me a minute to put this glass down. It's good to see you. Really good. You're staying for supper, I hope.
Put the glass on the table. We're not settling anything by shouting across the room. Take a breath, step back, and let the other person finish. You can disagree without frightening everyone else.
I found an old photograph while clearing a drawer. Half the people in it I haven't seen for years. Funny how a small bit of paper can bring back the sound of a whole room.
